claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 9 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 9 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex

circumstances: Child is not in local authority care
Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by accessing the assessment guidelines.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I can see we need to start by understanding the age of the child or children you're claiming for.

**To get started, could you tell me:**

1. **How many children are you asking about?**
2. **What are their names and dates of birth (or current ages)?**

This will help me determine which assessment path to follow, as Child Benefit eligibility depends significantly on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Automatically qualifies (if other conditions are met)
- **16-19**: May qualify if still in education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Please provide these details and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that context. So you have one son, **Alex, who is 9 years old** and lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex is under 16, he qualifies for that category. Now let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment to check the other eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This is a standard check - most children under 16 won't be working, but I need to confirm this for Alex.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 9, so he's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's what I expected for a 9-year-old. Alex is in school and not working, so that's a clear "yes" to that requirement.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any specific benefits in his own right:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(For a 9-year-old in primary school, this would be unusual, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 9-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's what I expected. Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits, so that's another "yes" to that requirement.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This check is about apprenticeships. Since Alex is only 9 years old and still in primary school, this won't apply to him. But let me confirm:

**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

For context, this would typically only apply to older teenagers, so I expect the answer is "no" - but let me verify.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. He's only 9 and in primary school, so no apprenticeship at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not in any apprenticeship, so that requirement is satisfied.

Let me continue to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives with you in the UK. Let me confirm your situation:

**Which of the following best describes your residency status?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and you're in one of these situations: working, seeking work, have sufficient resources, studying, or family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Since you've indicated you're in the UK with your son, I expect option 1 applies - but please confirm your residency situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, option 1 - I normally live in the UK. We live here and this is our home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check that you're responsible for Alex. You've already told me he lives with you, which is the key requirement here.

**To confirm - does this apply to you:**

You **live with Alex** - he's your son and lives in your home with you, correct?

(This is the primary way responsibility is established, and you've already indicated this is the case.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which clearly establishes your responsibility for him. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any dispute about who should be claiming?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is there any shared custody arrangement where another person might be claiming?
- Have you and anyone else agreed who should be the primary claimant?

Please let me know your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only person claiming for Alex, which means there's no conflict or dispute. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You've mentioned he lives at home with you, but let me confirm:

**Which of the following applies to Alex:**

1. **Living normally at home with you** (he's in school and lives in your household)
2. **Currently in hospital** (as an inpatient)
3. **In care** (e.g., in a care home or similar institution)
4. **Fostered** (in a foster placement)

I expect option 1 applies based on what you've told me, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, option 1 - he's living normally at home with me. He goes to school during the day and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final check. I need to confirm:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- You're paying for Alex's accommodation, food, and living costs yourself (not the council)
- The council is not providing financial support for his care

This would be the case for most families - please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm the one providing for him and paying for everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's the final requirement confirmed. You're providing for Alex yourself, and the council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance.

Based on my assessment of your situation, I can now provide you with the outcome:

reasonings: Alex is 9 years old (under 16), which automatically qualifies him for Child Benefit eligibility. He is not in paid work (he is in primary school). He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right. He is not in any disqualifying apprenticeship. You normally live in the UK, satisfying residency requirements. You live with Alex and are responsible for him. You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, with no disputes. Alex is living normally at home with you. You are paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance, and the local council is not paying towards these costs. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. He meets all the key requirements: he is under 16 years old, not working, not receiving other benefits, living with you in the UK, and you are providing for his care. The local council is not involved in paying for his upkeep. You can proceed with your Child Benefit application."
